translations.translatedText: # Saturday 5.2.2022 (radio)
Demonstration. Health care fees. Moving. Runeberg Day. Runeberg Literature Prize.
## Demonstration in Helsinki

![The movement known as Convoy Finland held a protest in central Helsinki on Friday 4 February.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_4987,h_2805,x_5,y_382/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-91086561fd93601d00b/1644008832)
Open image viewer
Convoy demonstration blocked a road in Helsinki. Photo: Silja Viitala / Yle

A big demonstration has kept the police busy in Helsinki. The Convoy demonstration started on Friday evening in central Helsinki. The demonstrators are opposing corona restrictions and high fuel prices.
The demonstrators parked many dozens of cars on Mannerheimintie, so that the road became blocked. The police had to tow cars away so that the road could be opened.
During the night the police arrested 55 demonstrators who did not obey police orders. Demonstrators also gathered in central Helsinki on Saturday afternoon.
## Health care fees

![Pirkkala health centre, with a health centre road sign in front of it.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_3396,h_1910,x_1,y_297/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-90011761dc1730a859a/1641813980)
Open image viewer
Health centre fees can be big for people who have very little money.  Photo: Marko Melto / Yle

More and more Finns are not paying doctors' fees and other health care fees. If fees are not paid, they are transferred to enforcement, that is, the fees are taken from the person's salary or pension.

Last year about half a million health care fees were transferred to enforcement. The number has doubled in 10 years. The reason is that there are more people in Finland than before who have very small incomes. For example, people on an unemployment pension, long-term unemployed people or disabled people have very small incomes.
Social sector expert Anne Perälahti tells Yle that the new wellbeing services counties must consider whether health care fees can be removed for poor people.
## Desire to move
![Moving boxes are being transported.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_5254,h_2955,x_0,y_164/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-5039005b76b909ed9ed/1535968250)
Open image viewer
During a move, things are packed into moving boxes. Photo: Derrick Frilund / Yle
Many Finns are thinking about moving to another place. The Finnish Municipal Development Centre has asked Finns whether they want to move to another place.

About 20 per cent of Finns say they may move to another place within 2-3 years. Many Finns want to change place to get a better home and living environment. Nature and safety are also reasons to move to a new place.
The desire to move is greatest in southern Finland, and the least desire to move is in small rural municipalities.
## Runeberg Day
![Runeberg statue in Porvoo.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_5568,h_3132,x_0,y_583/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-770346601c3c8d30e1b/1732028336)
Open image viewer
Johan Ludvig Runeberg statue in Porvoo. Photo: Tiina Jutila / Yle
Runeberg Day was celebrated on Saturday. Johan Ludvig Runeberg is Finland's national poet.
The Finnish national anthem *Maamme* is a poem by Runeberg.
Runeberg lived in the 1800s. He was Swedish-speaking and wrote in Swedish. Runeberg Day is celebrated on 5 February, because it is Runeberg's birthday.
## Runeberg Literature Prize
![Author Quynh Tran at Runeberg's home in Porvoo.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_1969,h_1107,x_0,y_102/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-91014161fbb5abcd24b/1643886122)
Open image viewer
Author Quynh Tran won the Runeberg Prize for her book Varjo ja viileys. Photo: Outi Paappanen
Today the Runeberg Literature Prize was also awarded.

This year the Runeberg Literature Prize goes to debut author Quynh Tran for the novel *Skugga och svalka*. In Finnish, the title of the book is *Varjo ja viileys*. The book tells about a family that has come to Finland from Vietnam.
The Runeberg Literature Prize is 20,000 euros.
